interactions.content: Meeting notes: Maya gave an overview of the platform. Rahul Mehta is looking for rapid implementation, emphasized that current manual processes are a bottleneck. Sarah Chen joined for the last 10 minutes to understand high-level ROI. Mentioned budget cycles run in Q4. Action Item: Maya to send technical documentation and arrange a deep dive.

Email thread: Hi Rahul, attached is the API documentation and architecture overview as discussed. Please let me know if your team has any questions prior to our technical deep dive next week. Best, Maya

Meeting notes: Walked through the API integration. Rahul seemed very excited about the webhooks capability. He noted that their current tech stack is primarily Python and React. We confirmed full compatibility. Rahul asked for a proposed implementation plan to present to Sarah.
key_facts: Tech stack is Python and React

interactions.content: Meeting notes: Presented the $180,000 annual contract. Sarah Chen pushed back immediately, stating that predictable cost boundaries are her primary concern and $180k is at the absolute top of their potential range. She requested a detailed breakdown of implementation costs versus recurring licensing.

Meeting notes: Presented the standard 6-week rollout plan. Rahul expressed serious concerns. He stated that a 6-week timeline is too slow for their Q3 objectives and they need core features live in 3 weeks. Maya committed to reviewing the timeline with the delivery team to see if phases can be accelerated.
key_facts: Rahul thinks 6 weeks is too slow

interactions.content: Email thread: Hi Sarah, here is the detailed breakdown of the $180,000 annual cost, separating the one-time implementation fees from the ongoing licensing. Note that we have applied a first-year discount to keep it within the boundary.

Meeting notes: Both Sarah and Rahul joined. The 6-week implementation plan was officially rejected. Rahul stated they cannot commit unless we can get core functionality live faster. Sarah reiterated that the pricing is still slightly too high given the timeline risks.

Meeting notes: Maya proposed a phased rollout: Phase 1 (core features) in 2.5 weeks, Phase 2 in 4 weeks. Rahul liked this approach. Sarah noted that this mitigates some risk and agreed to review revised pricing terms if this timeline is guaranteed in the contract.
Email thread: Hi team, attached is the updated proposal reflecting the phased rollout. Rahul, the SLAs for Phase 1 are included. Best, Maya
Meeting notes: Rahul confirmed that the technical team accepts the phased rollout plan. We agreed to move forward with this structure. They asked how we manage communication during implementation.
Meeting notes: Established a weekly update preference for all stakeholders during the rollout. Maya committed to sending a comprehensive status report every Friday afternoon to both Sarah and Rahul.
Meeting notes: Deep dive into Phase 1. Rahul approved the data mapping. No blockers identified.

Meeting notes: Sarah and Maya discussed final numbers. Maya offered a slight reduction in implementation fees to $175,000 total for year one to close the gap. Sarah agreed this fits their predictable cost boundaries.
Meeting notes: Sarah formally accepted the $175,000 pricing structure. Legal review is the next step.
Email thread: Hi Sarah and Rahul, here is the weekly update. Legal review is progressing. Phase 1 prep is on track.

Meeting notes: Sarah noted that weekly updates are too frequent for her now that pricing is settled. She requested a preference change: weekly updates should transition to bi-weekly executive updates for her, but technical updates can remain weekly for Rahul.
Email thread: Hi Sarah, confirming I will shift your updates to bi-weekly starting next week. Rahul, I will keep you on the weekly technical distribution.
Meeting notes: Rahul and Maya synced on API keys. Everything is ready for the kickoff.

Meeting notes: Discussed the final timeline. Rahul mentioned they have a hard October deadline for Phase 1 to align with a major product release on their end. The exact final timeline is still pending legal sign-off on the MSA.
Email thread: Hi Rahul, just checking in on the MSA status so we can finalize the timeline for the October deadline. Let me know if legal needs anything from our end.
key_facts: Waiting on legal to finalize timeline

preference_changes.context: Technical updates remain weekly, executive updates moved to bi-weekly.

rejections.reason: NovaTech rejected it because they needed a faster initial deployment and preferred a phased rollout.

interactions.content: Meeting notes: Met with Lisa Wong. She is looking to improve operational efficiency across their smart grid monitoring systems. Deal size estimated at $95k. She mentioned David Park will need to heavily vet any solution for SOC 2 compliance.
key_facts: SOC 2 compliance is critical for David Park

interactions.content: Meeting notes: David Park joined. Very security-first mentality. He spent 45 minutes grilling us on data encryption at rest and in transit. We committed to providing our latest SOC 2 Type II report and architecture diagrams.
Meeting notes: Lisa reviewed the workflow automation features. She is very pleased with the potential efficiency gains. Decision process is slower here due to security reviews.
Meeting notes: David reviewed the SOC 2 report. He had follow-up questions about our incident response plan. Maya provided the requested policies on the call.
Meeting notes: David specifically asked about granular audit trails for user actions. Maya demonstrated the audit logging features in the platform. David seemed satisfied.

Meeting notes: Lisa and David joined. We discussed communication preferences post-sale. David stated they prefer monthly executive updates rather than weekly, as their internal review cycles are longer.
key_facts: Preference for monthly executive updates established

interactions.content: Email thread: Hi David, as requested, here is the whitepaper detailing our KMS integration and key rotation policies. Best, Maya
Email thread: Hi Maya, we have completed our security review. I am passing the approval to Lisa to finalize the operational budget. - David
key_facts: Passed to Lisa for budget approval

Meeting notes: Elena reviewed EHR sandbox integration. Confirmed compatibility with Epic & Cerner HL7/FHIR APIs.
Meeting notes: Governance board moved status call preference from bi-weekly to monthly compliance reviews due to physician shift schedules.
